name: Miko Pawlikowski
title: Keynote: 7 Deadly Traps of SRE
abstract:
Site Reliability Engineering was never meant to be about firefighting, yet too many teams find themselves stuck in an endless cycle of pages, postmortems, and quick fixes. Why? Because SRE is full of hidden traps — patterns that look like best practices on the surface but slowly erode reliability, burn out engineers, and stall progress.

In this talk, we’ll expose the 7 Deadly Traps of SRE, from the obsession with chasing “five nines,” to the cult of on-call heroism, to the false comfort of tooling and checklists. For each trap, we’ll unpack why it’s so seductive, how it quietly sabotages your team, and what to do instead.

You’ll walk away with a clearer lens on the pitfalls holding SRE organizations back, and a practical playbook to help your team escape firefighting mode and reclaim the true purpose of SRE: building systems - and cultures - that are resilient, scalable, and human-friendly.
bio: Miko Pawlikowski is an SRE Author and a platform engineer at Quadrature. He has led large-scale infrastructure and SRE initiatives at Citadel and Bloomberg, with deep expertise in Kubernetes, cloud computing, and chaos engineering. Passionate about building resilient systems and communities, he brings together engineers worldwide through conferences and media projects.

name: Dan Putman
title: The Runtime Gap: Why Your AI Agents are Flying Blind and How to Fix It
abstract:
The adoption of Generative AI in the SDLC has created a paradox: code generation has outpaced safe production. As teams shift from coding to prompting, they now spend up to 70% of their time verifying and fixing bugs. Traditional observability often comes too late, requiring reactive redeployments that stall innovation.

This session explores the mandatory shift toward AI Site Reliability Engineering. We will discuss how to move beyond "unknown unknowns" by providing AI agents with In-line Runtime Context. You will learn how to:

* __Shift Left Reliability__ : Integrate real-time code insights into the design and early SDLC phases to prevent incidents before they occur.
* __Empower AI Agents__: Use dynamic instrumentation to give agents line-level visibility, turning statistical guesses into verified root cause analysis.
* __Eliminate Technical Toil__ : Slash MTTR by moving from weeks of troubleshooting to live resolution in minutes without redeploying code.
bio:
Dan Putman is a Solution Architect at Lightrun with a distinguished career in software development and engineering management. Prior to his current role, Dan served as the VP of Engineering at Pillar Technology, where he led a massive team of over 250 technologists and pioneered innovative technical quality programs. He is also the Co-Founder and former CTO of Direct Energy Partners.
With deep technical expertise spanning medical research, logistics, and renewable energy, Dan is known for tackling the complex "unknown unknowns" that impact global organizations. He focuses on implementing strategic, high-impact solutions that enhance developer productivity and system resilience. Dan is committed to advancing the future of AI-driven site reliability, helping enterprises transition from reactive firefighting to proactive, runtime-aware engineering.
